about.summary: I hold a Bachelor of Software Engineering from FPT University, Can Tho (2023–2026) and work across the full software development lifecycle: turning requirements into specs and acceptance criteria, designing APIs and data models, building and testing services, then deploying and maintaining them. I've done this in a company team at Rikkeisoft, in group projects, and on AnSite, a platform I took from idea to deployment. I adapt quickly to new stacks and domains, from .NET and Node.js to Python and mobile integration, and I use AI coding agents inside a disciplined workflow: plan first, review every change, test before merge. The projects below show the details.
feat.ansite.title: AnSite: Camera-Based Safety Platform for Factories
feat.ansite.meta: Lead Developer | Capstone Project & Startup | NestJS, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Socket.IO, React, Python, MediaMTX, Docker, Caddy, GitHub Actions
feat.ansite.b1: Split the system by workload: a Python edge agent on the factory LAN handles camera streams and YOLO/VLM detection, while a NestJS cloud API owns the database, so heavy AI load cannot take down the dashboard.
feat.ansite.b2: Diagnosed a concurrency bug where a lock held during slow work (image processing, uploads) blocked config updates for 71 s; narrowing the lock cut the delay to under 0.4 s, with a regression test.
feat.ansite.b3: Built the NestJS alert ingestion API with idempotent writes (retries with the same event ID never duplicate an alert), composite PostgreSQL indexes for per-organization queries, and real-time push via Socket.IO rooms.
feat.ansite.b4: Delivered alerts beyond the dashboard: each alert keeps its evidence image and is pushed to a Zalo bot with the photo, re-sending identical bytes on retry.
feat.ansite.b5: Secured live camera viewing: the API issues short-lived HMAC-signed session tokens, and the MediaMTX gateway checks every stream request against an internal auth endpoint (kept off the public internet behind Caddy) before a viewer gets video.
feat.ansite.b6: Gave every edge device its own credential, stored as a SHA-256 hash and verified in constant time, and wrapped activation and revocation in database transactions so each one either completes fully or changes nothing.
feat.ansite.b7: Hardened the API with role-based guards on organization-scoped data, input validation (class-validator), Helmet security headers and rate limits, with stricter limits on login and device activation.
feat.ansite.b8: Deployed to a Linux VPS with GitHub Actions CI and 2,800+ automated tests across API, web and edge; changes follow a written plan with acceptance checks before AI agents implement them, then a separate review.
feat.eh.title: EventHub: Event Booking Platform
feat.eh.meta: Backend Developer | Personal Project | ASP.NET Core 8, EF Core, SQL Server, Ocelot, SignalR, Docker
feat.eh.b1: Decomposed event booking into 10 ASP.NET Core services (auth, events, categories, booking, vouchers, social, chat, chatbot, notifications, withdrawals), each with its own SQL Server database.
feat.eh.b2: Put an Ocelot API gateway in front of every service as the single entry point, forwarding JWT bearer tokens to protected APIs and routing both REST and SignalR traffic.
feat.cs.title: Calendar Shop: Mobile E-Commerce App
feat.cs.meta: Backend Developer | Team of 5 | ASP.NET Core 8, EF Core, SQL Server, OData, JWT, VNPay, Flutter
feat.cs.b1: Hardened the VNPay payment flow by verifying the callback signature, amount and current order state before marking an order paid, with a background worker that cancels orders left unpaid after 15 minutes.
feat.cs.b2: Designed one query endpoint per resource that lets the mobile app filter, page and pick fields itself, so new screens needed no new endpoints; queries compile to SQL that selects only the requested columns (OData, EF Core projection).
feat.cs.b3: Built JWT login with Google sign-in and rotating refresh tokens stored server-side: every refresh revokes the old token, and logout, password change or reset, and admin account lock revoke all of a user's sessions.
feat.cs.b4: Worked with the mobile team on the Flutter Dio client: on a 401 it makes a single refresh call, queues the other failed requests, then retries them all, so users stay signed in without duplicate refreshes.
feat.cs.b5: Standardized validation and errors (FluentValidation, RFC 7807 ProblemDetails) with Serilog logging.
exp.meta: Rikkeisoft | Ho Chi Minh City | VMS (Visitor & Manpower Management System)
exp.b1: Prevented cache stampedes in a shared Redis caching module for 4 NestJS services: a token-checked distributed lock lets only one request rebuild an expired entry while the rest back off with jitter.
exp.b2: Kept cached data correct after writes with version-based invalidation (one Redis counter per entity, hashed query keys); traced and fixed a bug where one write bumped versions several times and emptied the cache too often.
exp.b3: Built User Management end-to-end (NestJS API, DTOs, React admin page, unit tests).

journey.heading: My Journey
j1.title: Where my passion for technology began: level design for a player community
j1.text: From 2014 to 2018 I designed nearly 100 custom levels for the 2D platformer Plazma Burst 2, more than 30 of them highly rated by the community. Players came to me with their own requests, so I gathered their feedback, built each level around what they wanted and kept refining it. I became one of the game's best-known level designers and was invited to lead one of its largest player clans: my first experience of working directly with users and a community.
j2.title: Pre-university academic awards
j2.text: I took part in academic and English competitions through middle and high school, and ranked among the top 10 students every semester.
